title: heapq
short: Get the smallest item fast, again and again.
what: heapq keeps a plain list arranged as a min-heap: the smallest item always sits at heap[0]. Pushing and popping each cost O(log n). There is no max-heap, so you store negated numbers instead.
analogy: An emergency room line. Whoever is most urgent is always seen next, no matter when they arrived, and a new patient slots in without re-sorting everyone.

frames.label: heappush(heap, 5)
frames.say: heap = [] is a plain list. heappush(heap, 5) adds 5. Drawn as a tree, heap[0] is the root.

frames.label: heappush(heap, 3)
frames.say: Push 3: it lands at the end, is smaller than its parent 5, so they swap. 3 is the new heap[0].

frames.label: push 8, push 1
frames.say: Push 8, then 1. 1 climbs two levels to the top. A push climbs at most the tree height: O(log n).

frames.label: heappop(heap)
frames.say: heappop(heap) removes and returns the smallest, 1. The last item fills the root and sinks back down.

frames.label: max-heap: store -x
frames.say: No max-heap exists. Push -x instead: -8 is the smallest, so popping it and flipping the sign gives 8.

frames.label: (priority, item) drawn as 1,b
frames.say: Push (priority, item) tuples. They compare by the first item, so priority 1 comes out first with its item "b".

frames.label: heapify([9, 4, 7, 1])
frames.say: heapify(nums) turns [9, 4, 7, 1] into a heap in place in O(n), faster than pushing items one at a time.

frames.label: heapq.nlargest(2, nums)
frames.say: nlargest(2, nums) returns the top 2, largest first; nsmallest the bottom k. For one item use max() or min().

when: Always take the cheapest next item
Keep the top k while streaming
python:
import heapq
heap = []
for x in [5, 3, 8, 1]:
    heapq.heappush(heap, x)
print(heap)
print(heapq.heappop(heap), heap)
mx = [-x for x in [5, 3, 8]]
heapq.heapify(mx)
print(-heapq.heappop(mx))
tasks = [(2, "a"), (1, "b"), (3, "c")]
heapq.heapify(tasks)
print(heapq.heappop(tasks))
nums = [9, 4, 7, 1]
heapq.heapify(nums)
print(nums, heapq.nlargest(2, nums), heapq.nsmallest(2, nums))
watch: heapq is a min-heap only. For a max-heap push -x and negate what you pop.
heap[0] is the smallest, but heap[1] is not the second smallest. The list is not sorted.
On equal priorities Python compares the next tuple item. If those cannot be compared, add a counter: (priority, i, item).
